purpose.summary: Label a stable, descriptive attribute with a decorative colour theme, optionally as a two-part key/value pair with an icon and a dismiss action
useWhen: Labelling what something *is* — a category, scope, tier, environment, or marketing label — rather than what state it is in
Showing a key/value pair as one unit (pass both label and value; it renders as a split tag)
Displaying a removable filter or selection chip, using actionIcon plus onActionClick
doNotUseWhen: The value is system-driven and changes on its own, or the colour implies good/bad/waiting (use StatusBadge instead)
You need a keyboard-operable control — a clickable Tag is a div with no role and no tabIndex (see knownGaps)

shared.name: variant
shared.codeNote: Fill treatment. 'outline' uses the theme's outline background and border; 'secondary' uses its filled secondary background.

shared.name: size
shared.codeNote: Tag height and type scale. 'sm' also shrinks the action button from size '2xs' to '3xs'.

shared.name: theme
shared.codeNote: Decorative colour name, not a semantic status. Three values resolve to semantic colour sets internally: green→success, red→danger, yellow→warning. The prop value is still the colour name.
shared.figmaNote: Figma's theme variant names carry an emoji prefix ('⚫ gray', '🔵 blue'); Code Connect strips it. Figma exposes 13 of the 15 — 'forest-green' and 'lime' are code-only (see knownGaps).

shared.name: value
shared.codeNote: The tag's text, and the only required prop. In a single tag it renders as {value || label}; in a split tag it is the right-hand half.
shared.figmaNote: Bound to the Figma TEXT property 'text#1444:4'. Note the asymmetry: a one-part Figma tag's text maps to `value`, not `label`.

designOnly.name: icon
designOnly.notes: A boolean toggle that reveals the Figma icon slot, paired with the instance swap '↳ icon#1444:6'. Code has no boolean — the icon renders whenever the `icon` prop holds a name, so Code Connect derives this from presence.

codeOnly.name: label
codeOnly.notes: Passing label *and* value switches rendering to an internal two-tag split composite: label on the left, value on the right. Passing label alone renders a single tag whose text is the label. This mode switch is silent and changes which other props are honoured (see knownGaps).

codeOnly.name: icon
codeOnly.notes: An IconV2 name, rendered at size 'xs' before the text. In split mode it is applied to the left tag only — the right tag never takes a tag icon.

codeOnly.name: iconProps
codeOnly.notes: An IconPropsV2 object passed through to IconV2, excluding name, size, fallback and ref. Dropped entirely in split mode — Tag does not forward it to the split composite.

codeOnly.name: actionIcon
codeOnly.notes: An IconV2 name rendered inside a transparent icon-only Button after the text — the dismiss/remove affordance. In split mode it is applied to the right tag only.

codeOnly.name: onActionClick
codeOnly.notes: Fires on the action button. The handler calls stopPropagation() and preventDefault() first, so an action click never also triggers the tag's own onClick.

codeOnly.name: onClick
codeOnly.notes: Inherited from React.HTMLAttributes rather than declared, so it does not appear in TagProps' own members. Its presence implies hover styling and cursor-pointer. It is the one inherited attribute forwarded into split mode, where it is attached to both halves.

codeOnly.name: enableHover
codeOnly.notes: Applies hover styling to a non-clickable tag. Ignored in split mode: the split path overwrites it with Boolean(onClick), so a hoverable split tag requires an onClick.

codeOnly.name: rounded
codeOnly.notes: Switches the corner radius from the default to a full pill. In split mode the outer corners round and the shared inner edge stays square.

codeOnly.name: disabled
codeOnly.notes: Visual and cursor state only — it is not a CVA variant and sets no aria-disabled. The tag is a div, so there is nothing for it to disable; onClick still fires. It does disable the action Button.

codeOnly.name: title
codeOnly.notes: Native tooltip on the text span, defaulting to title || value || label so truncated text is always recoverable on hover. Dropped in split mode, where each half falls back to its own text.

codeOnly.name: className
codeOnly.notes: Additional classes on the tag root, or on the split wrapper in split mode. Should not override token-based styling.

codeOnly.name: labelClassName
codeOnly.notes: Classes for the left half of a split tag. No effect on a single tag.

codeOnly.name: valueClassName
codeOnly.notes: Classes for the right half of a split tag. No effect on a single tag.

bindings.transformNote: Figma prefixes each theme name with a colour emoji. The map is the complete set Code Connect handles; 'forest-green' and 'lime' have no Figma entry.
Figma's single text property maps to `value`, not `label` — a one-part Figma tag is a one-part code tag.
Boolean toggle in Figma; the icon *name* comes from the instance swap '↳ icon#1444:6' via executeTemplate(). Omitted when the toggle is off.

keyboardSupport: Tab — reaches the action button only, when actionIcon is set
Enter / Space — activates the focused action button
No keyboard path to the tag itself; role and tabIndex are omitted from TagProps and cannot be supplied
accessibility.notes: A single tag is a plain div with no role, so it is announced as text. The type deliberately omits 'role' and 'tabIndex', which means a Tag with onClick cannot be made keyboard-operable or announced as a control from the outside — use Button for anything that must be actionable. The action button is a real <button> and is focusable, but it renders with ignoreIconOnlyTooltip and an unlabelled icon, so it has no accessible name.

states.name: hoverable
states.description: Hover background and border shift (cn-tag-hoverable). Also applied implicitly whenever onClick is set, and in split mode only when onClick is set.

states.name: disabled
states.description: Disabled text colour and not-allowed cursor; suppresses hover styling and disables the action button. Applied via utility classes, not a CVA variant.

governance.tokenStatus: Layout, radius, size and split refs verified against tailwind-utils-config/components/tag.ts and the built stylesheet; theme refs record the colour *set* each theme resolves to, not the per-slot variables within it

knownGaps: TAG-001: A clickable Tag is not keyboard-operable. The type omits 'role' and 'tabIndex', so no consumer can fix it from outside — use Button when the thing must be actionable
TAG-002: The action button has no accessible name. It renders iconOnly with ignoreIconOnlyTooltip and an unlabelled icon, and Tag exposes no prop to label it

TAG-003: Split mode drops most inherited attributes. Passing label + value forwards only onClick to the split composite, so id, data-*, aria-*, title, iconProps and other HTMLAttributes are silently discarded
TAG-004: Split mode overrides enableHover with Boolean(onClick), so a caller's enableHover is ignored there
TAG-005: 'forest-green' and 'lime' exist in code but not in the Figma component's theme variant, so a design cannot specify them and Code Connect cannot produce them
TAG-006: 'children' is accepted by the inherited HTMLAttributes type but never rendered — the text comes from value/label only
TAG-007: 'disabled' sets no aria-disabled and does not stop onClick; it is visual state only
